grow_divide.doc:
Process base class.

A `Process` is a temporal unit of computation that operates on state and advances in time.
Each subclass must implement the `update()` method and optionally the `invoke()` method.

Processes are stateful and typically used for simulations of continuous or discrete dynamics.

_contract.summary: Exponential single-cell growth with size-threshold division — cells elongate then split in two at a length threshold.

inputs.agents: Cells; per cell: location (µm), length (µm), radius (µm), mass (pg), angle (rad), velocity (µm/s).

outputs.agents: Cells grown by rate (1/s) toward threshold (µm); at threshold, replaced by two daughters (division writes {_add, _remove}).

assumptions: Growth is pressure-modulated by `pressure_k`; optional per-division mutation of rate/threshold.

multibody.doc:
2D rigid-body physics for colonies — a pymunk space that integrates
rod-shaped cells, soft multi-segment cells, and circular particles under
collisions, damping, jitter, optional gravity/adhesion, and chamber walls.

Its structured ``contract`` (with per-port units) is assigned at the bottom
of this module alongside the other process contracts.

_contract.summary: 2D rigid-body physics for the colony — steps a pymunk space so cells grow, push apart, and reorient under collisions, damping, and jitter.

inputs.segment_cells: Rod-shaped rigid cells — per cell: location (µm), length (µm), radius (µm), mass (pg), angle (rad), velocity (µm/s).
inputs.bending_cells: Soft multi-segment capsule cells joined by rotary springs — per cell: location (µm), length (µm), radius (µm), mass (pg), angle (rad), velocity (µm/s).
inputs.circle_particles: Circular particles (e.g. EPS) — location (µm), radius (µm), mass (pg).

outputs.segment_cells: Rod cells after one physics step — position (µm) / angle (rad) advanced by forces + collisions.
outputs.bending_cells: Bending cells after one physics step (segment poses updated).

math: \Delta t_{sub} = \Delta t / N, \qquad x \leftarrow x + v\,\Delta t_{sub}
\text{collision: push bodies apart along } \hat{n} \text{ by the penetration depth } \delta

symbols.F: net force on a body (collisions + jitter + optional gravity/adhesion)
symbols.d: fraction of velocity retained per second (damping_per_second)
symbols.\\delta: overlap / penetration depth between two colliding bodies (µm)
symbols.\\hat{n}: contact normal (unit vector) along which overlap is resolved

assumptions: Overdamped motion (velocity damping/s, gravity off by default); `substeps` sub-steps per update; rectangular chamber of side env_size (µm) with walls of wall_thickness (µm).

remove_crossing.doc:
Step base class.

A `Step` is a stateless, non-temporal computational unit within a composite process.
It is triggered when its data dependencies are satisfied, functioning like a reaction
or transformation rule.

Override the `.update()` method to define custom behavior.

Override `.triggers()` to control which input ports trigger the step.
By default all inputs trigger — the step runs whenever any input changes.
To make some inputs "silent" (received but not triggering), return only
the triggering subset from `triggers()`.

Class attributes for memoization:
    ``_cache`` — ``'none'`` (default) or ``'by_hash'``. When
        ``'by_hash'``, ``invoke()`` hashes the Step's config and the
        incoming state, keys a class-level cache by
        ``(schema_version, hash)``, and reuses prior outputs on a
        hit. Requires ``_schema_version``.
    ``_schema_version`` — opaque string identifying the Step's
        output-relevant implementation version. Bumping invalidates
        all prior cache entries under the old version. Required when
        ``_cache == 'by_hash'``.

_contract.summary: Mother-machine-style culling — removes cells that cross a boundary (e.g. washed out past the open end of a trench).

outputs.agents: Cells minus any whose position crosses the [x_min, x_max] × [y_min, y_max] bounds (µm) or `crossing_y` (µm) line.

assumptions: A cell past the bound is removed outright (no partial retention).

multibody_viz.doc: End-of-run animated-GIF renderer matching the test-suite GIF style. Per ``accumulate(state)`` (once per tick): 1. Merge cells + particles into one layer, stamp the static field onto the frame so the heatmap overlay renders every tick. 2. ``GifRenderer.draw_frame(...)`` → PIL Image; append to internal ``self._frames`` (bounded FIFO by ``max_frames``). Once, in ``render()`` at end-of-run: 3. Quantize all accumulated frames (MEDIANCUT, 256 colors) and encode as an animated GIF in-memory (``disposal=2``, ``optimize=False`` — same pattern as ``simulation_to_gif``). 4. Return ``''``. Performance: the quantize + GIF encode runs exactly ONCE (in ``render``) rather than on every tick, so cost is linear in step count instead of O(n²). The ``max_frames`` cap still drops oldest frames FIFO to bound memory for long runs.

_contract.summary: Visualization Step — renders the colony as an animated GIF. Buffers one frame per tick from the cell/particle poses (optionally over a scalar field heatmap) and encodes them once at end-of-run into an inline data-URI GIF.

inputs.cells: Cells to draw — per cell: location (µm), length (µm), radius (µm), angle (rad), plus optional scalar (pressure / qs_state / inclusion_body) used for color.
inputs.fields: Optional 2D scalar field (concentration grid) drawn as the background heatmap.
inputs.time: Simulation time stamped on each frame (s).

outputs.html: A single HTML string with a base64 animated-GIF data URI of the whole run.

symbols.L: cell length (µm) — drawn as a capsule of this length
symbols.(u, v): pixel coordinates in the rendered frame
symbols.C(x, y): background scalar field value mapped through the colormap

assumptions: Pure rendering — reads state via wires and emits HTML; no state mutation. Color mode (uniform / pressure / qs_state / inclusion_body) and the field overlay are config flags.

cell_mass_traces.doc: Per-cell mass-over-time line plot. Configurable cell field (default 'mass').

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type
